call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer: Demonstrate industrial production methods and equipment for tandem solar cells and modules that combine efficiency gains with lifetimes comparable to silicon.
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · Scope
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer: Improve the prospects for selling durable, efficient tandem solar products at scale. The work supports European solar manufacturing and the joint solar research and innovation agenda.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · Expected Outcome

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer: This suits solar manufacturers, production-equipment suppliers and research institutes that can demonstrate industrial tandem-cell and module production. At least three independent grant recipients must be in different eligible countries, including one in a European Union Member State. One acts as coordinator (the partner representing the group). Control by China or a legal entity based there prevents participation.

cards.title: Innovation
cards.question: How new must the project be, and in what must it innovate?
cards.answer: Innovate in tandem cell and module technology, large-scale thin-film and interface engineering, and manufacturing processes or equipment that can scale.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · Scope

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The work should reach TRL 6–7 (technology readiness level: technology demonstrated in relevant or operational conditions) by project end. The call allows work to start at any maturity level.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Demonstration and integration of work
cards.question: Where must the solution be demonstrated, and how must the work fit with existing systems?
cards.answer: Demonstrate the tandem technology, thin-film and interface engineering, and production equipment at a scale that supports wider industrial deployment. Link the processing steps to the finished device’s efficiency and lifetime.
cards.sources: Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · Scope

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer: Higher-efficiency solar modules could affect the volume of generation connecting to TenneT’s network. The call focuses on cell and module production and gives no transmission-operator role.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
The Commission indicates EUR 28.5 million for tandem solar manufacturing. It expects 3 awards.
- Grant request: around EUR 9.5 million per project is indicative. The Commission can select a different request.
- Funding form: Budget-based grant (paid using approved costs or rates for the funded work).
cards.sources:
Horizon Europe Work Programme 2026–2027, Climate, Energy and Mobility · pp. 153–154 · Specific conditions

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
For-profit organisations can receive up to 70% towards tandem solar manufacturing.
- For-profit organisations: Up to 70% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow), leaving at least 30% to cover.
- Non-profit legal entities: Up to 100% of eligible costs (project costs the grant rules allow).

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
Apply for tandem solar manufacturing through the European Funding & Tenders Portal in one stage.
- Full proposal: 1 December 2027, 17:00 Brussels time. Submit Part A (online administration form) and Part B (technical proposal). Part B is limited to 40 pages.
- Opening: 4 August 2027.

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The grant agreement (the contract setting the funded work and payment rules) sets the start date and duration for tandem solar manufacturing.
- Required start: Work normally starts after the grant agreement is signed. A reasoned exception needs approval.

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
An industrial tandem-solar proposal needs a credible commercial strategy where the results will be sold or deployed.
- Conditional — Commercial exploitation: If results are intended for commercial exploitation, include an exploitation strategy. The plan should include a business case and steps for scaling, commercialisation and deployment.
- Expected: Report results to European Partnership for Innovation in Photovoltaics (the solar industry and research partnership) for monitoring of its performance indicators.
- Exception — Results transfers: The granting authority may object to transfers or exclusive licences (giving another party sole rights to use the results) of results for up to four years after project end.
